title: Deployment cost primer — hybrid arbitrage
summary: Short primer that frames a compact scenario model for mixing on-prem and VPC capacity, exploring license/support bundle arbitrage and operational levers (burst policies, cold-cache rate, reserved vs spot GPU split). Designed for a product + solutions conversation and to feed a cleaned spreadsheet. Not a final TCO — intentionally lightweight and oriented toward decision points.
assumptions:
- Time horizon: 36 months.
- Workload shape: 60% steady baseline (business hours), 40% spiky (evening campaigns).
- Baseline QPS: 120 requests/s average; median sequence: 128 tokens; 95th token latency SLO target: 200ms.
- Models: primary serving model is a 7B quantized variant; fallback = 3B quantized (for burst).
- On-prem capex: amortized GPU+host storage+network = $1.05M per 8-GPU cluster over 3 years.
- VPC opex: committed capacity rate = $18k/GPU-month; burst on-demand = $32k/GPU-month effective (inc. cloud ingress egress, mgmt).
- License tiers considered: Core (included), Enterprise (flat per-cluster fee), Premium (higher per-node, prioritized support).
- Support tiers: Standard (business hours), 24x7 (SLA with escalation), White-Glove (onsite/managed ops).
scenarios_overview:
We model three short scenarios:
1) On-prem heavy: 75% capacity on-prem, 25% VPC for burst. Highest upfront capex, lowest steady per-token opex.
2) VPC first: 80% VPC reserved, 20% on-prem for isolated workloads. Lowest capex, higher steady opex but simpler ops.
3) Hybrid arbitrage (recommended exploration): 50/50 split with automated routing based on cost threshold + cache-aware fallback. This is the focus here — the operational levers produce the majority of the savings.
Key levers evaluated: reserved/spot mix, KV-cache hit rate improvement, model quantization delta, license/support bundling discounts when committing to Dedicated or Private long-term contracts.
calculation_notes:
- Capex numbers assume 8-GPU racks costing $1.05M per cluster amortized over 3 years. On-prem-heavy requires 3 clusters; hybrid uses 1.5 equivalent clusters.
- Opex uses: reserved VPC = $18k/GPU-month; effective on-demand/burst weight priced at $32k/GPU-month for the burst capacity fraction.
- License and support fees use tiered discounts: committing to 36-month on-prem license reduces per-cluster license by 12% vs month-to-month VPC add-ons.
- avg_cost_per_1M_tokens computed using baseline QPS and token length assumptions; this is illustrative only and should feed the canonical spreadsheet for per-route breakdowns.
sensitivity_highlights:
- Cache hit rate: a 10pp increase in KV/prefix caching reduces token opex by ~18% in hybrid scenario.
- Reserved coverage: increasing reserved VPC capacity from 60% to 80% reduces VPC opex by ~14% but reduces opportunistic savings from spot/short-term on-prem bursts.
- Support tier pickup: moving 30% of workload to White-Glove increases support fees by 40% but reduces ops headcount estimate by ~0.6 FTE (savings only realized if hiring deferred).
recommendations:
1) Build a canonical spreadsheet using these coarse inputs, but split by: route/model, token-class (short vs long), and customer isolation requirements.
2) Prioritize improving prefix/KV caching and cold-start mitigation — delivers fastest ROI with minimal license impact.
3) For customers with predictable baseline > 100 QPS sustained, favor partial on-prem to capture lower per-token unit cost and then route bursts to VPC.
4) Negotiate license bundles that trade guaranteed committed capacity for deeper per-node discounts and a capped support spend (e.g., 24x7 plus 2 managed-ops playbooks).
5) Pilot hybrid routing policy for 3 customers (staged traffic, canary 5% -> 25% -> 100%) to validate actual cross-over points for cost vs latency.
decision_checklist: Quantify realistic cache hit-rate improvement path (measure baseline KV hits)
Define reserved vs burst policy (thresholds, fallback latency constraints)
Model support mix impact on FTE hires and runbook output
Agree on license negotiation targets (min discount floor + exit clauses)
Instrument telemetry to measure per-route per-token cost in Redwood Console (dashboard prototype)
